cell_types.name: Neural crest cells
cell_types.summary: Neural crest cells are a transient migratory population that arises at the border between neural plate and non-neural ectoderm and goes on to make peripheral neurons and glia, melanocytes, and craniofacial cartilage, bone and smooth muscle. hPSC-derived neural crest is used as the common entry point to sensory neurons, Schwann cells, melanocytes and enteric neurons, and to model neurocristopathies.
cell_types.maturation_note: SOX10 reporter expression appears around day 6 and peaks near day 11 in dual-SMAD-inhibition plus WNT protocols; cells can be sorted on p75/HNK1 or SOX10 and then expanded for many passages before lineage differentiation.

morphology.endpoint: A loose, non-epithelial sheet of small stellate to spindle-shaped cells with several short processes, far less tightly packed than the starting colonies. Patches of residual neuroepithelium or rosette-like whorls are common and are the main contaminant you will see.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat compact colonies of small cells with sharp borders, replated at low density so single cells and small clusters are still visible.

stages.label: Neural plate border epithelium
stages.look: A confluent, uniform epithelial sheet with no clear colony edges; nuclei are densely packed and the sheet looks featureless at low power.

stages.label: Early neural crest
stages.look: Cells loosen and become stellate with short processes, and begin to crawl over one another; the sheet looks grainier and less epithelial than at day 4.

stages.label: Migratory neural crest
stages.look: Clearly migratory stellate and spindle cells spread across the dish. Any remaining tight rosettes or bright neuroepithelial whorls mark residual CNS-type cells.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost; Hackland et al. report loss of OCT4 by day 7 in their defined protocol.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: The core neural crest readout; SOX10 reporter lines are the standard way to score these protocols.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: Surface marker used for FACS enrichment. Not specific on its own: it is also expressed by neural cells, so pair it with SOX10 or HNK1.

markers.name: B3GAT1
markers.note: Marks a subset of early crest; Bajpai et al. found only about 30% of migratory cells HNK1+ while 95% were SOX9/p75/AP2a+.

markers.name: TFAP2A
markers.note: Neural plate border and crest marker; retained in non-neural ectoderm too, so read it with GATA2/3.

markers.name: PAX3
markers.note: Border marker; co-expression with SOX10 is good evidence of genuine crest identity.

markers.name: PAX7
markers.note: Co-expressed with SOX10 in the day-7 cultures of the top-down inhibition protocol.

markers.name: SNAI2
markers.note: EMT/migration programme; induced as cells leave the epithelial sheet.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Expressed by about 95% of cells migrating out of attached rosettes in the Bajpai method.

markers.name: ETS1
markers.note: Cranial crest marker; detected at day 7 in the top-down inhibition protocol.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Should be low. High SOX2/PAX6 means the culture drifted to central neuroepithelium.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Menendez et al. report under 5% PAX6+ cells in a good run of the BIO/SB431542 protocol.

markers.name: GATA3
markers.note: With GATA2, flags non-neural ectoderm, which is what you get if BMP signalling is too high.

functional_assays: Migration out of attached rosettes or spheres
Differentiation into peripheral neurons, glia and mesenchymal progenitors
In ovo grafting into chick dorsal neural tube
qc: SOX10 and p75 co-expression by flow at day 7-11
PAX6 under 5% of cells (BIO/SB431542 protocol)
Loss of OCT4 by day 7
Confirm tri-lineage potential: peripheral neuron, glia, mesenchymal progenitor

protocols.name: SBio: WNT on, Activin/Nodal off (single step, chemically defined)
protocols.principle: Activating canonical WNT with a GSK3 inhibitor while blocking Activin/Nodal and TGF-beta with SB431542 pushes hPSCs straight to neural crest without a rosette intermediate or cell sorting.

source.authors: Menendez L, Yatskievych TA, Antin PB, Dalton S
source.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
source.title: Wnt signaling and a Smad pathway blockade direct the differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells to multipotent neural crest cells

protocols.efficiency: Over 90% of treated cells positive for neural crest markers; under 5% PAX6+
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs maintained in a defined medium containing heregulin-beta, Activin A, LR-IGF and FGF2. Dissociate and plate at 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2 to start differentiation.

stages.name: Neural crest specification
stages.base_medium: Chemically defined maintenance medium with Activin A omitted

factors.name: SB431542
factors.role: ALK4/5/7 inhibitor; blocks Activin/Nodal and TGF-beta

actions: Plate dissociated hPSCs at 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2
Switch to defined medium without Activin A containing BIO and SB431542
Feed daily and watch the sheet lose its epithelial look from about day 6
stages.checkpoint: By day 12 most cells should be p75+/HNK1+/AP2+ with few PAX6+ cells

stages.name: Expansion of neural crest stem cells
stages.base_medium: Same defined medium with BIO and SB431542
stages.feeding: Daily medium change; passage aggregates with Accutase
actions: Passage with Accutase once cultures are dense
Keep expanding in the same two small molecules; the paper reports over 25 passages (more than 100 days) without losing potency
stages.checkpoint: Cells keep p75/HNK1/AP2 expression and can still make peripheral neurons, smooth muscle and mesenchymal precursors

materials: Chemically defined hPSC medium without Activin A
poly-L-ornithine and laminin for downstream neuron plating
tips: The step-by-step version of this method with troubleshooting is published as Menendez et al., Nat Protoc 2013;8:203-12 (PMID 23288320, doi 10.1038/nprot.2012.156), which quotes about 15 days to neural crest stem cells.
Noggin is not needed: the authors report no major effect when it is omitted.
Daily feeding matters; this is a single-step protocol with no medium switches to rescue a starved culture.
pitfalls: Seeding density changes the CNS-versus-crest balance, so keep 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2 constant between runs.
The paper reports results with BIO; CHIR99021 is used at much lower doses in other defined protocols, so do not transfer the 2 µM number to a different GSK3 inhibitor.
unverified: Matrix for the neural crest step itself is not specified in the paper (Geltrex is used for hPSC maintenance and for other steps)
Full base medium formulation is not given in the text
Exact p75+/HNK1+ percentages appear only in the flow cytometry figures
Passage interval and split ratio during expansion are not stated

protocols.name: Top-down inhibition (TDi): BMP4 saturation plus DMH1, xeno-free
protocols.principle: Endogenous BMP4 varies between runs and between lines, which makes neural crest yield erratic. Flooding the culture with BMP4 to saturate the response and then dialling the signal back down with the BMP type-1 receptor inhibitor DMH1 fixes BMP activity at the level crest needs, whatever the cells secrete.

source.authors: Hackland JOS, Frith TJR, Thompson O, Marin Navarro A, et al.
source.title: Top-Down Inhibition of BMP Signaling Enables Robust Induction of hPSCs Into Neural Crest in Fully Defined, Xeno-free Conditions

protocols.efficiency: Reproducible SOX10 induction across WA09, Shef6 and Miff-1; without TDi the same medium gave 5-80% p75++ cells between runs
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1 on Matrigel. Seed at 10,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in E6 medium with 10 µM Y-27632 and leave 24 h before switching to induction medium.

stages.name: Seeding

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; survival after single-cell seeding

actions: Dissociate hPSCs to single cells
Seed at 10,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in E6 with Y-27632
stages.checkpoint: Evenly scattered attached single cells, no dense clumps

stages.name: Neural crest induction with top-down inhibition

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: saturates the BMP response so endogenous BMP4 no longer sets the dose

factors.name: DMH1
factors.role: BMP type-1 receptor inhibitor; attenuates the saturating signal to the level crest needs

actions: Switch to NCN2 with all four factors 24 h after seeding
Culture 7 days without passaging
Score p75 and SOX10 at day 7 by flow cytometry
stages.checkpoint: Day 7 cells positive for p75 and HNK-1 with TFAP2A, PAX3 and SOX10 expression and loss of OCT4

tips: BMP4 activity differs between suppliers and lots: titrate your BMP4 in the presence of 1 µM DMH1 and pick the dose where crest induction saturates.
Varying BMP4 between 13 and 17 ng/mL did not change SOX10 induction, so the window around 15 ng/mL is forgiving.
The CHIR99021 and SB431542 doses here are 5-fold and 10-fold lower than in BSA-containing protocols; do not carry doses across media.
Day 7 cells can be moved to non-adherent culture on 1% agarose in N2-supplemented DMEM/F12 with ROCK inhibitor for the first 24 h.
pitfalls: Using DMH1 alone or BMP4 alone fails: DMH1 alone leaves PAX3/PAX6/SOX2 neural cells, BMP4 alone induces GATA2/GATA3 non-neural ectoderm.
Noggin was repressive in this system, so BMP-ligand traps are not interchangeable with the receptor inhibitor.
Heterogeneity persists even with TDi: expect some rosette-like structures and non-SOX10 cells at day 7.
The authors could not generate MITF+ melanocytes from TDi crest, so check downstream potency for your lineage of interest.
unverified: Numerical day-7 SOX10+ percentage for TDi (reported in figures, not in the text)
Whether melanocyte competence is lost under TDi, which the authors leave open

protocols.name: Rosette outgrowth: migratory crest from attached neuroectodermal spheres
protocols.principle: hESCs are taken through suspension neuroectodermal spheres that contain neural rosettes. The spheres attach, crest-like cells crawl out, and the rosettes are dissected away, giving a crest population without sorting.

source.authors: Bajpai R, Chen DA, Rada-Iglesias A, Zhang J, et al.
source.title: CHD7 cooperates with PBAF to control multipotent neural crest formation

protocols.efficiency: About 95% of migratory cells SOX9+, p75+ and AP2-alpha+; about 30% HNK1+
protocols.start_requirements: WA09 (H9) hESCs on Matrigel with irradiated MEFs in medium with 8 ng/mL bFGF. Depleted of MEFs and Matrigel, then harvested as clusters with 1 mg/mL collagenase IV for 30-40 min.

stages.name: Neuroectodermal sphere formation
stages.base_medium: NIM: DMEM/F12 and Neurobasal 1:1 with 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27, 5 µg/mL insulin, penicillin-streptomycin
stages.feeding: Suspension culture in uncoated polypropylene dishes
actions: Transfer hESC clusters to NIM in uncoated polypropylene dishes
Let spheres form and rosettes develop inside them
Allow spheres to attach spontaneously to the dish
stages.checkpoint: 50-80% of spheres attach between days 6 and 9

stages.name: Crest outgrowth and rosette removal
stages.feeding: As spheres attach; medium as above
actions: Watch for stellate cells migrating away from the rosette clusters between days 6 and 9
Dissect the rosettes away with a 28G needle under an inverted microscope, leaving the migratory cells behind
Passage these P0 crest cells with Accutase onto 1 µg/mL fibronectin
stages.checkpoint: Migratory cells are NESTIN+ but lack nuclear SOX2, and are about 95% SOX9/p75/AP2-alpha positive

stages.name: Mesenchymal progenitor conversion (optional)
actions: Replate P0 crest on 1 µg/mL fibronectin and keep in NIM for 10-15 days to mature into mesenchymal progenitors
For spontaneous differentiation instead, plate on 100 µg/mL ornithine plus 5 µg/mL laminin in growth-factor-reduced medium (DMEM/F12 and Neurobasal 3:1 with 0.25x B27) and feed weekly
stages.checkpoint: Mesenchymal progenitors can be driven to adipocytes and osteoblasts

materials: Matrigel and irradiated MEFs for hESC maintenance
tips: A second crop (P1) of crest can be collected by re-plating the dissected rosettes and harvesting the cells that migrate out again.
This method needs no FACS, which is useful when you want crest from a line with no reporter.
pitfalls: Only 50-80% of spheres attach, so yield per experiment varies.
Incomplete rosette dissection leaves SOX2+ neuroepithelium that will overgrow the crest.
The original culture used MEF feeders and is not xeno-free.
unverified: Exact day the cultures are considered finished (the paper gives a window of days 6-9 for migration, with analysis at 1, 4 or 7 weeks of further differentiation)

cell_types.notes: Protocols disagree about BMP: some require BMP inhibition for crest, others are repressed by it, and endogenous BMP4 output differs between lines and even between runs of the same line, which is exactly what the top-down inhibition method was built to control. Yield is also density-dependent, so fix your seeding density first. SOX10 reporter lines make these protocols far easier to score; with a wild-type line, use p75 together with SOX10 or HNK1 rather than p75 alone, since p75 is also expressed by neural cells. Expect residual neuroepithelium in every method.

cell_types.name: Sensory neurons (nociceptors)
cell_types.summary: Sensory neurons of the dorsal root and trigeminal ganglia detect pain, temperature, itch and touch; nociceptors are the small-diameter subset carrying TRP channels and NaV1.7-1.9. hPSC-derived sensory neurons are used for analgesic screening, channelopathy and neuropathy modelling, and for studying human-specific mechanosensation.
cell_types.maturation_note: BRN3A/ISL1 neurons by day 12 and NTRK1 in over 60% of cells by day 10; peripherin is ubiquitous by day 15, ion channels (SCN9A/10A/11A, P2RX3, TRPV1, TRPM8) are up by day 15, and ganglion-like clusters with substance P and CGRP appear by day 30.

morphology.endpoint: Small round, bright, phase-dense cell bodies sitting on top of the culture with long thin neurites forming a dense web. By a month the somata drift together into ganglion-like clumps linked by thick neurite bundles.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Compact colonies grown to confluence before induction; borders still sharp.

stages.label: Neuralised sheet
stages.look: A dense, uniform sheet of small cells with no colony structure; almost all cells are nestin-positive at this point.

stages.label: Young neurons on a crest bed
stages.look: Round phase-bright cell bodies with one or two thin processes appear above a flatter layer of crest-like cells; the neurites are short and sparse.

stages.label: Neurite network
stages.look: A connected mesh of long neurites between bright, rounded somata; the flat background layer is thinning out.

stages.label: Ganglion-like clusters
stages.look: Somata gathered into dark clusters joined by thick fascicles of neurites, like small ganglia in a dish.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone by the end of the first week.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Marks the obligatory crest intermediate: 80% SOX10::GFP+ by day 12 under LSB3i. Residual SOX10+ precursors should be below 5% after passaging.

markers.name: TUBB3
markers.note: Pan-neuronal; about 75% TUJ1+ with the three-inhibitor cocktail, lower (33-40%) in some iPSC lines before passaging.

markers.name: POU4F1
markers.note: With ISL1, the pair that makes these neurons sensory rather than CNS; homogeneous by day 12.

markers.name: ISL1
markers.note: Read together with BRN3A.

markers.name: NTRK1
markers.note: Over 60% of cells by FACS at day 10; also the handle for sorting to enrich nociceptors.

markers.name: PRPH
markers.note: Peripheral rather than central identity; ubiquitous in BRN3A/ISL1 cells by day 15.

markers.name: SCN10A
markers.note: Nociceptor-selective sodium channel; up by day 15 along with SCN9A and SCN11A.

markers.name: P2RX3
markers.note: Strongly induced; the dominant phenotype in LSB3i cultures is P2RX3-positive.

markers.name: TRPV1
markers.note: Induced by day 15 but weaker than P2RX3; only some cells respond to capsaicin.

markers.name: PIEZO2
markers.note: Required for rapidly adapting mechanically activated current in hPSC touch receptors; the readout for mechanosensory subtypes.

markers.name: TAC1
markers.note: With CGRP, seen in over 60% of neurons at day 30 after NTRK1 sorting.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Marks the CNS fate you get without WNT activation; should be absent.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Abolished by the three-inhibitor cocktail; its persistence means the culture went central.

functional_assays: Calcium imaging with capsaicin, AITC, menthol or alpha,beta-meATP
Whole-cell patch clamp for TTX-sensitive action potentials
Piezo-driven mechanical indentation for mechanically activated currents
Cold and heat ramp responses
qc: Over 60% NTRK1+ by flow at day 10 (LSB3i)
BRN3A and ISL1 co-expression in the neuronal population
Residual SOX10+ precursors under 5% after passaging
Voltage-gated sodium currents and evoked action potentials in patch clamp

protocols.name: LSB3i: dual-SMAD inhibition plus three small molecules (accelerated nociceptors)
protocols.principle: Dual-SMAD inhibition neuralises hPSCs; adding a WNT agonist with FGF and Notch inhibition from day 2 diverts the culture through a SOX10+ neural crest intermediate and compresses nociceptor differentiation into about ten days.

source.authors: Chambers SM, Qi Y, Mica Y, Lee G, et al.
source.title: Combined small-molecule inhibition accelerates developmental timing and converts human pluripotent stem cells into nociceptors

protocols.efficiency: About 75% TUJ1+ neurons; over 60% NTRK1+ by FACS at day 10; 33-40% TUJ1+ in two iPSC lines before passaging
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated to single cells, pre-plated on gelatin for 30 min to remove MEFs, then plated on Matrigel at 20,000-40,000 cells/cm2 in conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/mL FGF-2 and 10 µM Y-27632. Start induction when fully confluent.

stages.name: Dual-SMAD inhibition (neuralisation)
stages.base_medium: KSR medium: Knockout DMEM with 15% Knockout Serum Replacement, 1 mM L-glutamine, 100 µM NEAA, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
actions: Begin only when the monolayer is fully confluent
Add LDN-193189 and SB431542 in KSR medium
stages.checkpoint: Over 95% of cells become nestin-positive under dual-SMAD inhibition

stages.name: Three-inhibitor nociceptor induction
stages.base_medium: KSR medium stepped into N2 medium in 25% increments every other day from day 4 (100% N2 by day 10)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; WNT agonist, the key factor for crest and neuronal conversion

factors.name: SU5402
factors.role: FGF/VEGF/PDGF receptor inhibitor; speeds crest fate choice

stages.feeding: Daily feeds; N2 added in 25% steps every other day from day 4
actions: Add the three inhibitors on day 2 and keep them to day 10
Stop LDN-193189 and SB431542 after day 5
Shift the medium from KSR towards N2 in quarter steps from day 4
stages.checkpoint: PAX6 is abolished and TUBB3+ neurons appear by day 10; over 60% NTRK1+

stages.name: Maturation and long-term culture
stages.feeding: Long-term culture in N2 with the three neurotrophins
actions: Passage to a lower density, which promotes maturation and removes most SOX10+ progenitors
Optionally sort NTRK1+ cells to enrich nociceptors
Keep in N2 with NGF, BDNF and GDNF; expect ganglion-like clusters by day 30
stages.checkpoint: Peripherin ubiquitous by day 15; ion channel expression (SCN9A/10A/11A, P2RX3, TRPV1, TRPM8) up by day 15; substance P and CGRP in over 60% of sorted neurons by day 30

materials: Knockout DMEM and Knockout Serum Replacement
tips: CHIR99021 is the load-bearing factor: with CHIR plus one of the other two you still get 53-58% neurons, with either alone you get few.
Passaging bulk cultures raises neuronal yield in slower lines, so a low day-10 count is often a timing lag rather than a failed run.
Sorting on NTRK1 is the cleanest way to get a defined nociceptor population for pharmacology.
pitfalls: Starting before the monolayer is fully confluent costs efficiency.
Lines differ substantially: two iPSC lines gave 33% and 40% TUJ1+ where hESCs gave 75%.
Cultures skew to P2RX3-positive, TRPV1-negative neurons, so do not assume a capsaicin response in every cell.
RUNX1 is broad at day 8 but falls by day 15, which does not match mouse data; treat subtype assignment with care.

protocols.name: NGN2 plus BRN3A transcriptional programming (inducible, CLYBL safe harbour)
protocols.principle: Doxycycline-inducible co-expression of NGN2 and BRN3A from a single cassette in the CLYBL safe-harbour locus converts iPSCs directly into a homogeneous sensory neuron subtype in two weeks, with no small-molecule patterning; running the same induction on neural-crest-derived cells yields two further subtypes including low-threshold mechanoreceptors.

source.authors: Nickolls AR, Lee MM, Espinoza DF, Szczot M, et al.
source.title: Transcriptional Programming of Human Mechanosensory Neuron Subtypes from Pluripotent Stem Cells

protocols.efficiency: Reported as a homogeneous culture of a single sensory neuron subtype; no percentage given in the text
protocols.start_requirements: An iPSC line engineered with a doxycycline-inducible NGN2-T2A-BRN3A cassette inserted at both CLYBL alleles (TALEN-mediated), maintained on Matrigel in E8 with daily feeds and split every 4-6 days with Accutase plus 10 µM Y-27632 on the day of passage.

stages.name: Induction
stages.base_medium: NDM: DMEM/F12 and Neurobasal 1:1 with GlutaMAX, B27 and N2

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: survival after single-cell plating; can be removed on day 1

stages.feeding: Optional day-1 medium change to drop Y-27632
actions: Dissociate iPSCs with Accutase and plate 20,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in NDM with doxycycline
Expect pluripotent morphology to break down and division to stop about 48 h after doxycycline
stages.checkpoint: Cells separate from one another and stop dividing by about 48 h

stages.name: Replating and process outgrowth

factors.name: BrdU
factors.role: eliminates any remaining dividing undifferentiated cells

stages.feeding: Medium change every other day through day 8
actions: Dissociate with Accutase on day 2 and seed 50,000 cells/cm2 on 0.1% polyethylenimine plus 15 µg/mL laminin
Add BrdU on day 4 only if undifferentiated cells persist
stages.checkpoint: An elaborate process network over the following 5 days

stages.name: Neurotrophin maturation
stages.feeding: Every other day to day 8, then half-volume changes
actions: Add the four neurotrophins from day 8
Keep doxycycline until day 14, then stop
Use for calcium imaging or patch clamp from day 21
stages.checkpoint: By day 14 a stable uniform neuronal culture with large rounded somata; functional recordings from day 21

tips: Use clones with the cassette in both CLYBL alleles; the authors did, to get robust expression.
Doxycycline before day 14 is needed: earlier withdrawal lowered efficiency and increased death.

For the neural-crest route, make spheroids in AggreWell 400, then plate in NDM with bFGF, EGF and 10 µM SB431542 (SB431542 stopped from day 6); crest cells migrate out after 1-2 weeks and are replated at 40,000 cells/cm2 as a new day 0. One day of doxycycline plus 50 nM retinoic acid from day 0 gives the low-threshold mechanoreceptor subtype.
pitfalls: This needs a genome-engineered line, so it is not a drop-in protocol for an arbitrary patient iPSC.
The subtype produced by direct induction has not been observed in mice, so mouse data may not transfer; the authors validated it against adult human DRG.
A transgene-free small-molecule protocol gives a different subtype mix, so results are not interchangeable with LSB3i.
unverified: Purity as a percentage (described as homogeneous but not quantified in the text)
bFGF and EGF concentrations for the neural-crest variant are stated in the paper as 20 µg/mL, which is inconsistent with usual ng/mL usage and looks like a unit error in the source

cell_types.notes: Two very different routes: small-molecule patterning through a crest intermediate (fast, works in any line, mixed subtypes, skewed to P2RX3+ TRPV1-low nociceptors) and transcription-factor programming (homogeneous, needs an engineered line, subtype set by the factor combination). Line-to-line variability in the small-molecule route is large, and passaging is part of the protocol rather than an optional clean-up step: it removes residual SOX10+ progenitors and raises neuronal yield. Schrenk-Siemens et al. (Nat Neurosci 2015;18:10-16, PMID 25469543, doi 10.1038/nn.3894) is the reference for PIEZO2-dependent mechanotransduction in hPSC-derived touch receptors and is worth reading alongside these; its culture details were not confirmed in this session.

cell_types.name: Schwann cells
cell_types.summary: Schwann cells are the myelinating and non-myelinating glia of the peripheral nervous system; they wrap axons, speed conduction and secrete neurotrophic factors. hPSC-derived Schwann cells and their precursors are used for myelin repair and nerve regeneration studies, for Charcot-Marie-Tooth and neurofibromatosis modelling, and as a feeder for axon growth.
cell_types.maturation_note: Schwann cell precursors are homogeneous by day 18 (over 99% SOX10+) and can be expanded for more than 35 passages; converting them to Schwann cells takes about a further 7 days, and myelin segments appear only after about 28 days of co-culture with dorsal root ganglion neurons.

morphology.endpoint: Long, slender bipolar cells with two tapering processes, aligned in parallel swirls and often in loose bundles, looking more like a fibroblast culture that has been combed than a random spindle culture.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies replated on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel before the medium switch.

stages.label: Neural rosettes
stages.look: Radial rosettes with bright centres within a dense neuroepithelial sheet; this is the point of replating.

stages.label: Elongating precursors
stages.look: Cells become elongated and slender, leaving the rosette pattern behind; the culture looks increasingly uniform.

stages.label: Schwann cell precursors
stages.look: A highly homogeneous, fast-dividing population of thin bipolar cells; almost every nucleus is SOX10-positive.

stages.label: Schwann cells
stages.look: Longer, flatter bipolar cells arranged in parallel arrays, often in tight bundles.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be absent once the rosette stage is passed.

markers.name: PAX3
markers.note: With TWIST and SLUG, marks the crest intermediate around day 5 of the second step.

markers.name: SNAI2
markers.note: Crest/EMT marker in the same window as PAX3.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Over 99% of cells SOX10+ at day 18 and expression persists through expansion; the key purity readout.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: Over 90% p75+ in the Liu et al. NCSC-derived route; used for FACS enrichment of the crest intermediate.

markers.name: S100B
markers.note: About 85% S100-beta+ after six weeks in the Liu et al. protocol.

markers.name: GFAP
markers.note: About 78% GFAP+ after six weeks (Liu et al.); also up in the Kim et al. Schwann cell step.

markers.name: PLP1
markers.note: Myelin protein expression rises on conversion from precursor to Schwann cell.

markers.name: PMP22
markers.note: Peripheral myelin protein; the gene behind CMT1A, so a key readout in disease models.

markers.name: MBP
markers.note: Only seen in co-culture: MBP+ segments after about 28 days with rat DRG neurons. Liu et al. detected MBP transcript at low level without co-culture.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Over 90% SOX9+ in expanded NCSCs (Liu et al.).

markers.name: GDNF
markers.note: One of several neurotrophic factors (with NGF, BDNF, NT-3, NT-4, CNTF) whose expression confirms functional glial identity.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Should be low; persistent PAX6 means the rosette stage went central rather than to crest.

functional_assays: Myelination co-culture with rat DRG neurons scored for MBP+ segments
Neurotrophic factor secretion
Sciatic nerve injury transplantation in vivo
qc: Over 99% SOX10+ by flow at day 18 (Kim et al.)
S100B and GFAP positivity after conversion
MBP+ myelin segments in DRG co-culture at about 28 days
Expansion stability: precursors should hold SOX10 over many passages

protocols.name: Two-step SCP route: SB431542 plus CT99021, then NRG1
protocols.principle: Six days of TGF-beta and GSK3 inhibition neuralises hPSCs into rosettes; simply adding neuregulin-1 to the same medium converts them into Schwann cell precursors, which expand indefinitely and can then be matured with forskolin, retinoic acid and PDGF-BB.

source.authors: Kim HS, Lee J, Lee DY, Kim YD, et al.
source.title: Schwann Cell Precursors from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells as a Potential Therapeutic Target for Myelin Repair

protocols.efficiency: Over 99% SOX10+ cells at day 18; no purification or sorting step needed

cell_types.notes: The practical difference between these two is the bank point and the timeline: the NRG1 two-step route gives a stable, expandable, near-pure (over 99% SOX10+) precursor at day 18 that you can freeze and return to, while the p75-sorted route needs FACS and six weeks of differentiation and ends at about 85% S100B+. Neither produces myelin on its own: MBP appears only in neuron co-culture, after roughly four weeks. If you are modelling a myelin gene (PMP22, MPZ), plan the co-culture from the start, since transcript-level readouts in monoculture will understate the phenotype.

cell_types.name: Melanocytes
cell_types.summary: Melanocytes are neural-crest-derived pigment cells that sit at the epidermal basement membrane and in hair follicles, making melanin in melanosomes and transferring it to keratinocytes. hPSC-derived melanocytes are used to model pigmentation disorders such as Waardenburg syndrome and Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome, to study melanoma initiation, and as a candidate cell therapy for vitiligo.
cell_types.maturation_note: In the dual-SMAD-inhibition route, melanoblasts are sorted at day 11 and the first pigmented cells appear about six days after sorting, with most clusters pigmented by day 20 and pellets visibly dark by passage five. The embryoid body route is much slower: pigment appears 3-4 weeks after the post-EB dissociation and most cells are pigmented 4-6 weeks after that.

morphology.endpoint: Dendritic cells with a small cell body and several fine branching processes, filled with brown-black granules. Confluent cultures look dusty brown by eye and the cell pellet is visibly dark.

cell_types.notes: The dual-SMAD route is faster and cleaner but needs FACS and a day-2 CHIR99021 start that is unforgiving by a day or two; the embryoid body route needs no sorting but takes two to three months and gives a mixed culture. cell_types.name: Keratinocytes
cell_types.summary: Keratinocytes are the surface-ectoderm-derived cells that build the stratified epidermis, dividing in the basal layer and differentiating upward into cornified squames. hPSC-derived keratinocytes are used to model epidermolysis bullosa and other genodermatoses, to build epidermal equivalents and skin grafts, and to test topical agents and irritants.
cell_types.maturation_note: Epithelial morphology dominates by about day 14 and keratinocyte-like cells with TP63 and KRT14 appear by day 24; in the retinoic acid/BMP4 route KRT14 reaches about 45% at day 30 and over 70% after the first passage. Terminal differentiation (KRT1, involucrin, filaggrin) needs high calcium or an air-liquid interface.

morphology.endpoint: A cobblestone sheet of small polygonal cells with bright, crisp borders growing in tightly packed islands that merge; cells at island edges are larger and flatter.

cell_types.name: Hair-bearing skin organoids
cell_types.summary: Skin organoids are cystic aggregates that co-induce surface ectoderm and cranial neural crest so that epidermis and dermis self-assemble, then produce pigmented hair follicles with sebaceous glands, Merkel cells and a sensory nerve network. They are used to study human hair follicle development, to model skin and appendage disease, and as a potential source of appendage-bearing grafts.

morphology.endpoint: A translucent cyst a few millimetres across with a smooth epithelial surface, a dense opaque core and, radiating outward, dozens of hair follicles with dark bulbs and visible shafts, plus a cartilaginous tail-like projection at one pole.

cell_types.name: Retinal pigment epithelium
cell_types.summary: The retinal pigment epithelium is a single pigmented hexagonal layer behind the photoreceptors that recycles retinoid, phagocytoses shed outer segments and maintains the outer blood-retinal barrier. hPSC-RPE is the most clinically advanced hPSC derivative, used in trials for age-related macular degeneration and Stargardt disease, and widely used for inherited retinal disease modelling and drug testing.
cell_types.maturation_note: Pigmented patches appear from about day 14 in directed protocols, but the hexagonal, transepithelial-resistant monolayer with RPE65, BEST1 and RLBP1 requires a passage and then roughly another month; Maruotti et al. detected those maturation markers about 60 days after their single whole-dish passage.

cell_types.notes: RPE is the easiest cell type in this slice to get and the easiest to over-claim: pigment at day 14 is not mature RPE. Expect to passage once, which both enriches (from roughly 50-80% to over 95% in both small-molecule protocols) and triggers the hexagonal polarised morphology, and then wait about another month for RPE65, BEST1 and RLBP1. Chetomin dose is strongly line-dependent and toxic above 20 nM in some lines. Check VSX2 is absent, since the neural retina is the competing fate, and remember that pigmented cells arising spontaneously in any hPSC culture are usually RPE, which is why RPE is also a contaminant to rule out when you are aiming at melanocytes.

cell_types.name: Retinal organoids (photoreceptors)
cell_types.summary: Retinal organoids are self-organising laminated neural retina containing all major retinal cell types, with photoreceptors that develop inner and outer segment structures and become light-responsive. They are used for inherited retinal degeneration modelling, photoreceptor transplantation research, gene therapy testing and studies of human photoreceptor development.
cell_types.maturation_note: Neural retina domains are picked at days 21-30; CRX and recoverin photoreceptors are present by about day 80, ARR3+ cones and NRL+ rods differentiate by about day 140, and outer-segment discs with light responsiveness need the better part of a year. Organoids can be held well past 400 days.

morphology.endpoint: A free-floating spheroid 1-2 mm across with a bright, optically clear laminated rim enclosing a darker core; at late stages the surface carries fine hair-like appendages where photoreceptor segments project outward.

cell_types.notes: These are long, manual, 3D cultures where the two things that actually determine success are the quality of the starting hPSC culture and your eye for which domains to dissect. Domain formation efficiency varies by line (62-88% in one study) and organoids from different lines reach the same developmental point on different days, which is why the morphological staging scheme matters more than the day count. Photoreceptor maturation is the slow part: markers by day 80-140, outer segments and light responses much later. The retinoic acid window is a real variable, with prolonged 1 µM exposure appearing to hold back opsin expression, and late-stage media in both open protocols contain serum, so they are not defined.

cell_types.name: Corneal epithelial cells
cell_types.summary: The corneal epithelium is the stratified surface-ectoderm-derived layer that forms the transparent front of the eye, maintained by limbal stem cells. hPSC-derived corneal epithelial cells are used to build transplantable epithelial sheets for limbal stem cell deficiency, and the SEAM system in which they arise is also a model of coordinated whole-eye development.
cell_types.maturation_note: Concentric SEAM zones appear at about weeks 3-4; non-epithelial zones are removed around week 7 and corneal epithelial progenitors are sorted at weeks 10-15; sorted cells then need a further 14-21 days to build a stratified sheet. The whole process is 100-120 days.

cell_types.notes: The SEAM is not a directed protocol in the usual sense: the colonies pattern themselves and your job is to recognise and physically isolate the right ring, which means this method rewards careful microscopy more than careful pipetting of growth factors. Laminin-511 E8 fragment is not interchangeable with other laminins here, since it was the only isoform that produced SEAMs in the authors' hands. Sorting is mandatory, with no single marker sufficient, and the whole thing takes three to four months. Because the same colony also makes retina, RPE and lens, always exclude RAX, MITF and crystallin-positive cells from the final sheet.

cell_types.name: Inner ear organoids (hair cells)
cell_types.summary: Inner ear organoids contain sensory epithelia with mechanosensitive hair cells bearing stereocilia bundles, supporting cells and associated neurons, resembling vestibular end organs. source.title: Generation of inner ear organoids containing functional hair cells from human pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: 90.9 ± 5.2% of Matrigel-embedded CHIR99021-treated aggregates formed vesicles; eGFP+ hair cells from day 39
protocols.start_requirements: WA25 hESCs or mND2-0 iPSCs cultured in Essential 8 or E8 Flex on recombinant human vitronectin-coated 6-well plates, passaged at 80% confluence or every 4-5 days at 1:10-1:20 with 0.5 mM EDTA in DPBS. Pluripotency checked by SOX2, OCT4 and SSEA-1 staining.

stages.name: Aggregation
actions: Dissociate with StemPro Accutase
Distribute 5,000 cells per well into low-adhesion 96-well V-bottom plates in E8 with Y-27632
stages.checkpoint: One compact aggregate per well after 48 h

stages.name: Non-neural ectoderm induction
stages.base_medium: CDM: F-12 with GlutaMAX and IMDM with GlutaMAX 50:50, plus 0.5% BSA, 1x chemically defined lipid concentrate, 7 µg/mL insulin, 15 µg/mL transferrin, 450 µM mono-thioglycerol

factors.name: FGF-2
factors.role: epithelialisation and ectoderm differentiation on the aggregate surface

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: low-dose BMP; needed for TFAP2A+ ECAD+ non-neural epithelium in mND2-0 iPSCs

stages.feeding: Transfer to low-adhesion 96-well U-bottom plates in 100 µL per well
actions: Move aggregates to U-bottom plates in 100 µL CDM with Matrigel, FGF-2, SB-431542 and (where needed) BMP4
This is differentiation day 0
stages.checkpoint: A TFAP2A+ ECAD+ non-neural epithelium on the aggregate surface

stages.name: Otic placode induction

factors.name: FGF-2
factors.conc: 50 ng/mL final (added as 25 µL of 250 ng/mL into the existing 100 µL)

factors.name: LDN-193189
factors.conc: 200 nM final (added as 25 µL of 1 µM)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.conc: 3 µM final (optional, day 8; added as 25 µL of 18 µM into 125 µL)
factors.role: optional WNT activation that may improve otic placode-like cell induction

stages.feeding: Add 25 µL CDM with factors on day 4; add 25 µL CDM on day 8
actions: On day 4 add FGF-2 and LDN-193189 in 25 µL to each well
On day 8 add a further 25 µL of CDM, optionally containing CHIR99021
Look for thickened outer epithelium relative to SB-only controls
stages.checkpoint: Thickened placode-like epithelium by day 12, reminiscent of otic placodes in vivo

stages.name: Matrigel embedding and otic vesicle formation
stages.base_medium: OMM: advanced DMEM:F12 and Neurobasal 50:50 with 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27 without vitamin A, 1x GlutaMAX, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: WNT activation; drives otic vesicle formation

stages.feeding: Complete medium change on day 15 with fresh 3 µM CHIR99021
actions: Pool day-12 aggregates, wash in OMM, resuspend in ice-cold undiluted Matrigel and place in about 25 µL droplets on a 100 mm plate
Incubate at least 30 min at 37 C, then bathe the droplets in 10 mL OMM with 3 µM CHIR99021
Alternatively plate aggregates individually in 24-well low-adhesion plates in OMM with 3 µM CHIR and 1% Matrigel
Image daily by DIC during days 12-18 and fix at least three aggregates on day 15 or 16 for PAX2/PAX8 staining
stages.checkpoint: Otic pit-like translucent bulges by day 15-16, confirmed PAX2/PAX8+; vesicles in 90.9 ± 5.2% of aggregates

stages.name: Floating maturation
stages.feeding: Spinner flask at 65 rpm, or 24-well plates on an orbital shaker at 65 rpm
actions: On day 18 wash the CHIR99021 out and move the droplets to floating culture with a wide-mouth P1000 tip
Transfer to 75 mL OMM in a 125 mL spinner flask on a stir plate at 65 rpm (up to 180 days), or 1 mL per well in 24-well plates on an orbital shaker at 65 rpm (up to 140 days)
stages.checkpoint: eGFP+ or MYO7A+ hair cells from day 39; sensory epithelia with ESPN+ stereocilia bundles and SOX2+/SOX10+/SPARCL1+ supporting cells

materials: 125 mL spinner flask and in-incubator stir plate or orbital shaker
N2 and B27 without vitamin A
tips: Both agitated formats (spinner flask and orbital shaker) gave similar results, so use whichever you have.
The day 15-16 PAX2/PAX8 check on a few sacrificed aggregates is worth doing: it tells you whether a four-month run is on track before you commit to it.
Matrigel embedding is doing mechanical work, not just signalling: aggregates in minimal medium without it produced migratory cells but no vesicles.
The CHIR99021 addition at day 8 is optional; the authors found it may improve otic placode-like induction but is not required.
pitfalls: BMP4 requirement is line-dependent: WA25 worked with SB alone (LSB over-inhibited), while mND2-0 iPSCs needed 2.5 ng/mL BMP4, so titrate per line.
Organoids also make epidermal epithelium (TFAP2A+ KRT5+), and as late as day 35 vesicles can be partly incorporated into it; this is part of the system rather than a failure.
The authors note two medium components that are poorly defined or imperfectly matched to human cells as a source of variability.
Hair cells resemble vestibular rather than cochlear cells, so this is not a cochlear hair cell model.
unverified: Numerical MYO7A+ percentage per organoid
Whether routine karyotyping was done (the authors state it was not, and instead kept passage number low)

cell_types.notes: A single well-specified protocol dominates this cell type, and it is demanding: four stages, a Matrigel embedding step, agitated long-term culture and a run length of two to six months. Two things decide the outcome. First, the BMP4 dose in the non-neural ectoderm step is line-dependent (one hESC line needed none, one iPSC line needed 2.5 ng/mL), so titrate before a long run. Second, the day 15-16 otic pit check on a few sacrificed aggregates is the only early readout you get. Expect epidermal epithelium alongside the otic vesicles, and expect vestibular-type rather than cochlear hair cells.
